title: Impact of Overtime Eligibility Expansion on Work Hours

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
I will use a Difference-in-Differences (DiD) approach. This is appropriate because we have a treatment group (employees newly eligible for overtime pay) and a control group (unaffected employees), observed before and after the policy change. The key identifying assumption is parallel trends - that treated and control groups would have followed similar trends in log hours worked in the absence of treatment.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s32_data.csv")

# Summary statistics
print("=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===")
print(summary(data))

# Check balance of observations across groups
print("=== SAMPLE COMPOSITION ===")
print(table(data$treated, data$post))

# Main DiD regression
print("=== MAIN DIFFERENCE-IN-DIFFERENCES RESULTS ===")
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = data)
print(summary(did_model))

# Extract and print the key coefficient
did_coefficient <- coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"]
did_se <- summary(did_model)$coefficients["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
did_pvalue <- summary(did_model)$coefficients["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]

print(paste("=== KEY RESULT ==="))
print(paste("DiD Coefficient:", round(did_coefficient, 4)))
print(paste("Standard Error:", round(did_se, 4)))
print(paste("P-value:", round(did_pvalue, 4)))

# Calculate group means for interpretation
print("=== GROUP MEANS ===")
group_means <- data %>%
  group_by(treated, post) %>%
  summarise(mean_y = mean(y), n = n(), .groups = 'drop')
print(group_means)

# Visualize the DiD design
print("=== CREATING VISUALIZATION ===")
plot_data <- data %>%
  group_by(treated, post) %>%
  summarise(mean_y = mean(y), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(group = ifelse(treated == 1, "Treated", "Control"))

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = post, y = mean_y, color = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(group = group), size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Difference-in-Differences: Log Hours Worked",
       x = "Period (0 = Pre, 1 = Post)",
       y = "Mean Log Hours Worked",
       color = "Group") +
  theme_minimal()

# Robustness checks
print("=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===")

# 1. Check for pre-treatment differences
pre_treatment <- data[data$post == 0, ]
pre_diff_test <- t.test(y ~ treated, data = pre_treatment)
print("Pre-treatment difference test:")
print(paste("Difference:", round(pre_diff_test$estimate[1] - pre_diff_test$estimate[2], 4)))
print(paste("P-value:", round(pre_diff_test$p.value, 4)))

# 2. Alternative specification with unit fixed effects (if multiple periods per unit)
# Check if we have panel structure
units_per_period <- data %>% 
  group_by(unit_id) %>% 
  summarise(periods = n_distinct(period))
if(any(units_per_period$periods > 1)) {
  print("Panel structure detected - running fixed effects model:")
  library(plm)
  panel_data <- pdata.frame(data, index = c("unit_id", "period"))
  fe_model <- plm(y ~ treat_x_post, data = panel_data, model = "within")
  print(summary(fe_model))
} else {
  print("Cross-sectional data - fixed effects not applicable")
}

# 3. Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
print("Robust standard errors:")
robust_results <- coeftest(did_model, vcov = vcovHC(did_model, type = "HC1"))
print(robust_results["treat_x_post", ])

print("=== ANALYSIS COMPLETE ===")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient on the DiD interaction term (treat_x_post), with a magnitude around 0.1-0.3. This would indicate that overtime eligibility expansion increases log hours worked by 10-30%. The economic intuition is that when workers become eligible for overtime pay (typically 1.5x regular wage), they have stronger incentives to work additional hours, leading to an increase in total hours worked. The effect size should be meaningful but not extremely large, as there are practical limits to how much additional work employees can take on.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log hours worked before and after the policy change between treated and untreated groups.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The expansion of overtime eligibility significantly increased the log hours worked.
